newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish yields edge down in short trade session.
newsitem.headline: Swedish yields edge down in short trade session.

text.p: Swedish bond yields fell during Friday's short trading session, largely on firmer markets in Germany and the United States.
The nine-year government bond yield fell by four basis points to 7.26 percent, while the six month T-bill rate fell by two basis points to 4.57 percent.
"Lower yields in Germany and U.S. took the Swedish yields lower as soon as the session opened" one dealer told Reuters, describing trade as thin and quiet.
The crown was unchanged from Thursday's close at 4.3325 against the mark.
Dealers said the Riksbank intervened in the market to defend the crown, although no levels were specified.
Next week has plenty of information with market-moving potential.

The government EMU-commission presents its report on Monday. On the same day, the National Debt Office offers market players the chance to convert their three-year government bonds to the "new" 10-year government bond loan.
